skills.name: The way of life of early humans

note.text:
Early humans (in the Old Stone Age, or Palaeolithic) lived by hunting animals, fishing and gathering wild fruits, roots, nuts and honey. They were nomads: they moved from place to place following animals and the seasons.
They made tools from stone, bone and wood: hand axes, scrapers, spears.
The discovery of fire was very important. Fire gave warmth and light, cooked food, kept wild animals away and helped make better tools.
They wore animal skins, lived in small groups (bands), shared food, developed language, and painted on rock walls.
Implications: better tools and fire gave more food and safety; working together helped groups survive; slowly people learnt more about plants and animals, which later led to farming.

worked_example.problem: Give three ways in which fire changed the life of early humans.
steps: Fire cooked food, making it softer, safer and easier to digest.
Fire gave warmth and light at night.
Fire kept wild animals away from the camp.
worked_example.answer: Cooking, warmth and light, protection from animals.

cards.idea: Early humans were hunters and gatherers, and nomads who moved with the animals and the seasons.
example: They gathered fruits, roots and honey, and hunted antelopes.

cards.idea: They made tools of stone, bone and wood, such as hand axes and spears.
example: A hand axe was a stone shaped by striking it with another stone.

cards.idea: Fire gave warmth, light, cooked food and protection from wild animals.
example: Cooked meat is softer and safer to eat.

questions.prompt: How did early humans get their food?

right.text: by hunting, fishing and gathering wild plants

wrong.text: by farming large fields of maize
wrong.explain: Farming came later, in the New Stone Age.
There were no markets or money.

wrong.text: by keeping cattle in big ranches

wrong.explain: There were no towns or shops.

Fire helped early humans cook their food.
Early humans painted on rock walls.
